decisions.reason: The disputed final bullet explicitly refers to the distinct published deferred-catalogue item rem-baire-category-choice-strength, and that item really does assert ZF strictness. The present ledger instead states that the ZF reversal remains open, so there is no cross-item contradiction in the rejected carrier.

The original verification used the infinitude of the odd set to deny cofiniteness, although an infinite subset can be cofinite, and cited zero's membership in the even set as evidence that the odd set is nonempty. The repaired proof instead uses one as an odd witness and the infinitude of the even complement.

The AC equivalence itself followed from the compact-T1 equivalence, but the extra comparison with compact Hausdorff products did not. The repair declares and cites the existing ZF theorem equating compact-Hausdorff product compactness with BPI.

Fact F3 was a conditional implication whose antecedent was absent from the Example and Given clauses, so compactness could not be inferred in ZF. The compact-T1 product hypothesis is now stated explicitly before the FIP argument uses it.

The pruning argument uses only that each retained menu is a subset of a finite menu, but L3 attributed this to unrelated definitions instead of the declared subset-of-finite theorem. The repaired invariant also explicitly controls closures, which is what the later closed-set construction needs.

For Kuratowski coding each ordered pair of points lies in the second relative level, but the set of all such pairs lies in the third. The source repeats the off-by-one claim; correcting it does not alter the final omega-plus-41 bound because the pure rational codebook already requires the much higher omega-plus-30 level.

Tachtsis Theorem 5.5 transfers BPI and Countable Choice simultaneously with injectively boundable conjuncts; it does not license Countable Choice as a stand-alone exceptional clause. The statement and proof now expose only plain injectively-boundable transfer, BPI transfer, and the simultaneous BPI-plus-Countable-Choice form.

The original prose asserted rank capture without giving the ZFA-provable equivalence required by its own boundability interface. The replacement writes the normal non-Urysohn formula explicitly, bounds every subset, topology subfamily, real-open set, and candidate function graph below one fixed segment, and proves both directions of relativization.

The displayed title asserted unconditional syntactic nonprovability, but an inconsistent ZF proves every sentence. The statement and contradiction proof correctly assume Con(ZF), so the title now carries exactly that metatheoretic consistency qualification.

The title omitted the Con(ZF) premise that appears in both the statement and proof. Without it an inconsistent ZF would prove Urysohn's lemma along with every other sentence, so the unconditional title was logically stronger than the established result.

The assertion that the complete-metric Baire principle has exactly the strength of DC is correct, but the ledger originally supplied only the weaker ZF theorem for separable complete metric spaces. The repair declares and cites the existing published ZF equivalence for unrestricted complete metric spaces.

The cover itself was well-ordered, but the construction compared arbitrary indices without defining any induced index order; duplicate indexing makes such an inference especially invalid. The repair indexes the closed refinement directly by cover members and uses the declared well-order throughout.

The cited metrization lemma requires a normal Moore space, not merely a T1 space with a sigma-cellular base. The theorem already assumes normality and the Moore property, so its conclusion remains valid; the repaired application cites those hypotheses and removes the false claim that normality was unused.

F1 did overstate clause (3b), but the rejection's claim that the needed club can fail at countable cofinality is false here. Because E contains only cofinality-omega ordinals, a cofinal omega-sequence of successors is a closed unbounded set disjoint from E. The repair separates this automatic case from the genuine clause-(3b) case.

F1 inaccurately omitted the uncountable-cofinality qualification from the local HYP interface. The main implication nevertheless uses the separately proved ladder-separation lemma, which handles countable-cofinality limits automatically and invokes (3b) only at uncountable cofinality. The dependency restatement and use description are now exact.

The limit points of a club need not be club when the ambient ordinal has cofinality omega, so the original all-beta proof was invalid. The local HYP clause asks only about beta of uncountable cofinality; there acc(C_beta) is club, and square_kappa(E) immediately contradicts a point of E in that club. The repaired proof establishes exactly the needed clause.

Containing the club of multiples of omega does not make E intersect omega-squared stationary, because the successor-shifted multiples form a disjoint club. This error occurred only in a remark; the direct countable ladder-separation proof remains valid. The remark now states that the local HYP (3b) is vacuous below omega-one and records both clubs.

The item openly identifies itself as a repackaging theorem and correctly instantiates every HYP clause from the more technical Dodd-Jensen supplier. Having the same eventual conclusion as a dependency is not a logical defect: this carrier provides the concise public implication and introduces no false step or unsupported strengthening.

The semantic existence of some inner model did not supply the fixed class formula or uniform effective proof translation asserted in F2, so the original consistency proof was unsupported. The repair instead fixes a hypothetical finite target refutation first and uses one definable-class relativization only for its finite axiom support, which is sufficient for the stated external implication.

For n below the length of q, condition (11) can exclude q from every B(sigma), while the original singleton term included only shorter Q-levels; hence G_n was not an open cover and could not be a development. The repair includes every isolated singleton at every level and also corrects the associated T1, uniform-base, normality-reduction, and guarded-trace checks found during full review.

reviews.reason: The implication DC to DMC follows from the cited DC iff DMC plus countable finite choice theorem, and Morillon's Question 1 identifies DMC implies DC over ZF as open. The final bullet accurately flags a contradictory statement in a separate published catalogue item and does not attribute that claim to this page's local choice ledger.

In the cofinite topology an open nonempty set must have finite complement. The odd set is nonempty because it contains one, while its complement is the infinite even set, so the odd set is not open and the even set is not closed. This directly verifies the counterexample.

AC gives arbitrary compact product compactness by Tychonoff, while the reverse follows because compact T1 spaces are among arbitrary compact spaces and their product theorem implies AC. The separately cited BPI equivalence now supports the compact-Hausdorff comparison without entering either main implication.

Each repaired coordinate is compact T1 and each constraint cylinder is closed. Under the now-explicit compact-T1 product hypothesis, the product is compact; finite choice verifies the cylinder FIP, and any point in their total intersection supplies the required coordinatewise choice function.

DMC supplies finite successor menus, subset finiteness makes the pruned menus finite, and the strengthened induction places each retained closure inside the corresponding dense-open prefix. Their finite unions form nested nonempty closed sets, whose common point follows from countable compactness and lies in every dense open set.

The corrected hierarchy calculation puts X times X in the third relative level. Metric graphs still lie below omega plus 33, covers below level two over X, and finite injection graphs below omega plus 41, so every quantifier in the explicit non-point-finite-refinement formula remains uniformly captured by the claimed absolute bound.

Pincus transfers finite conjunctions of injectively boundable statements, and the exceptional interface used here permits adjoining BPI; Tachtsis supplies the stronger joint BPI-and-Countable-Choice clause. The repaired theorem no longer infers a Countable-Choice-only transfer from that joint result.

For B equal to the union of the four witness parameters, all subsets of X and topology subfamilies occur at the first relative level, while the fixed pure real topology and every graph from X to the reals occur below omega plus a fixed finite number. Thus omega plus omega captures the entire bounded formula, and opacity of X gives the typed atom-blind certificate.

Assuming Con(ZF), the cited relative-consistency result gives a ZF plus Countable Choice model where Urysohn's lemma fails. Since DMC implies Urysohn's lemma over ZF, that model fails DMC; therefore a ZF proof of DMC would contradict the model. The repaired title now matches this conditional argument.

Under Con(ZF), consistency of ZF plus Countable Choice plus failure of Urysohn's lemma rules out any ZF proof of Urysohn's lemma, since such a proof persists in every extension. The contradiction argument is sound and the repaired title now states the indispensable consistency condition.

The separable complete-metric Baire theorem is provable in ZF, while the unrestricted complete-metric Baire principle is equivalent over ZF to serial dependent choice. The added dependency proves both implications with the same nonempty-carrier and empty-space conventions used by the ledger.

For each development level and cover member U, the repaired closed set contains points first covered by U in the declared cover well-order whose level star lies in U. Least-member arguments then prove coverage, closure, and discreteness without requiring an unprovided order on a separate index set.

Screening each development cover yields a base that is a countable union of pairwise disjoint open families. Because X is assumed both normal and Moore, the cited lemma converts that sigma-cellular base to a sigma-discrete base and applies Bing metrization; no T1-only implication is used.

At uncountable-cofinality limit stages HYP (3b) supplies the disjoint club. At countable-cofinality stages an increasing cofinal sequence of successors is closed below the stage and misses E. With either club, Fleissner's same-gap and different-gap induction gives eventual coordinatewise ladder separation.

The repaired item states HYP (3b) only for beta of cofinality greater than omega. The ladder lemma then supplies eventual separation at every beta, using (3b) exactly where needed; the construction theorem consumes the cardinal-arithmetic clauses and that separation property to produce the normal nonmetrizable Moore space.

Dodd-Jensen covering supplies the singular strong limit and square/diamond package. For each beta of cofinality greater than omega, acc(C_beta) is club; if E reflected there, stationarity would put a member of E in acc(C_beta), contradicting the defining square_kappa(E) exclusion. This proves precisely HYP (3b).

CH supplies the cardinal arithmetic at kappa equal to omega, the nonzero countable limit ordinals form the required stationary E, and the explicit enumeration recursion eventually separates every pair of ladders. The corrected remark observes that HYP (3b) has no eligible beta below omega-one and no longer confuses containing a club with stationarity.

The repaired covering supplier gives a strong-limit kappa of countable cofinality, the required continuum equation, a cofinal cardinal sequence satisfying the power bounds, and a stationary E satisfying the qualified nonreflection clause. These are exactly the five HYP clauses, so the repackaging implication is sound as written.

An actual refutation of ZFC plus a measurable cardinal has finite axiom support Delta. The NMSC inner-model theorem supplies one nonempty definable class satisfying those fixed relativized axioms, and finite interpretation translates that one refutation to an NMSC refutation. No uniform class predicate or arithmetic-base proof-code map is claimed.

Every development level now contains every isolated singleton, so it covers Q and has singleton stars above a point's finite coordinate length; branch stars refine their nested basic neighbourhoods. The uniform-base argument supplies regular Moore metacompactness, the explicit diagonal reduction proves normality from the H_Z separations, and both guarded trace domains are verified before evaluation.
